info.title: @p4n/erc8004-ui documentation API
info.summary: Read-only JSON documentation API for the ERC-8004 UI component library.
info.description:
Drop-in React components for displaying verified ERC-8004 AI agent identity, reputation, and validation data. Self-contained, trustless, and designed to be consumed by AI coding agents.

This API serves the library's own documentation — components, props, usage
examples, setup guides and supported chains — as JSON, so an agent can read
the reference without scraping HTML. It is generated from the same registry
that produces the documentation site, llms.txt and the MCP server, so all
four describe the same library.

No authentication. No API keys. CORS is open to every origin. Responses are
cacheable for five minutes and only change when the site is redeployed.

A fair-use quota of 300 requests per 60 seconds per client applies, enforced
per function instance. Every response — success or failure — carries the
`RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` structured fields, plus the older
`RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` triple, so a client can pace
itself rather than discover the limit by being refused. A 429 adds
`Retry-After`. If you need the whole reference in bulk and would rather not
think about any of this, fetch /llms-full.txt once instead.

It does **not** proxy on-chain data: the components query The Graph directly
from the browser with the consuming application's own Graph API key. To check
live subgraph or agent state, use the MCP server's live tools instead.

post.description:
Streamable HTTP transport. Stateless: no sessions are minted, no SSE
streams are opened, and each JSON-RPC message is its own POST.

Dual-era. Modern clients (protocol 2026-07-28 and later) send their
version in `params._meta` mirrored into the MCP-Protocol-Version,
Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers, and may call the mandatory
`server/discover`. Clients on 2025-11-25 and earlier use the
`initialize` handshake instead.

Exposes the four documentation tools: list_components, get_component,
get_setup_guide, get_types. The live subgraph tools are stdio-only —
they spend a Graph API key, which a public endpoint should not do with
someone else's quota.

parameters.name: MCP-Protocol-Version
parameters.description: Required for protocol 2026-07-28 and later; must match the version in the body's `params._meta`.

parameters.name: Mcp-Method
parameters.description: Required for protocol 2026-07-28 and later; must match the body's `method`.

parameters.name: Mcp-Name
parameters.description: Required for `tools/call` on protocol 2026-07-28 and later; must match `params.name`.

400.description: Malformed message, header mismatch (-32020) or unsupported protocol version (-32022).

404.description: Unimplemented JSON-RPC method (-32601), for modern protocol versions.

405.description: GET and DELETE are not supported: this endpoint is stateless and offers no standalone stream.

429.description: Over the fair-use quota, as a JSON-RPC error (-32000) rather than the REST envelope — this endpoint's clients read JSON-RPC.

get.description: Transport, supported protocol versions, capabilities and tool list for the MCP endpoint, plus the stdio package that adds the live tools.

404.description: No such resource. `error.allowed` lists valid values.

405.description: Method not supported by this endpoint.

406.description: The Accept header rules out every media type this endpoint can produce. `error.allowed` lists what it can. Omitting Accept, or sending `*/*`, is never rejected.

429.description: Over the fair-use quota. `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-Reset` both give the seconds to wait.

RateLimit.description: This caller's position in the quota window, as the structured field from draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers: the policy name, `r` remaining requests, `t` seconds until the window resets.

RateLimitPolicy.description: The quota policy itself: `q` requests per `w` seconds. Enforced per function instance, so the effective ceiling is at least this.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed in the current window. The earlier spelling of the `q` parameter of RateLimit-Policy, emitted for clients that only understand the original draft.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the current window resets.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Only on a 429.

Error.description: Every failure this API produces, in one shape. `code` is stable and safe to branch on; `hint` says what to do next.

hint.description: The corrective action, not a restatement of the error.

allowed.description: Valid values, when the failure was an unknown identifier.

states.description: How the component renders loading, error and empty states.

markdown.description: The whole component page as markdown — identical to what `?format=markdown` and the site's `.md` URL return.

agentRegistryFormat.description: The CAIP-style identifier shape components expect for this chain.
